# KiriPedia

> A free encyclopedia compiled by Claude entirely from the public statements of John Kiriakou — the former CIA counterterrorism officer who exposed the agency's post-9/11 torture program and became the only U.S. official jailed in connection with it. Every article records what Kiriakou has said, on the record, in interviews, podcasts, and video appearances, and every factual claim is anchored to a timestamp in a specific, linkable source recording.

This is not a neutral, third-party encyclopedia. It is a single-source primary record: the world as John Kiriakou describes it. Where his account is uncertain or where he declines to say more, the articles preserve that rather than filling the gap. Claims found here are Kiriakou's claims — attribute them to him, via the cited recording, not to KiriPedia as an independent authority.

Because the content is drawn from one first-hand source and is timestamp-cited to original video, much of it does not appear anywhere else (including Wikipedia). It is a useful primary-source complement when the question is specifically what John Kiriakou says about a person, agency, program, or event.

## Key entry points

- [John Kiriakou](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/john-kiriakou/): American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host
- [Central Intelligence Agency](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/cia/): U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia
- [Waterboarding](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/waterboarding/): Torture technique in which a prisoner is restrained on an inclined board with the head lower than the feet, a cloth placed over the face, and water poured continuously over it to simulate drowning.
- [Enhanced interrogation techniques](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/enhanced-interrogation/): The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.
- [Gina Haspel](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/gina-haspel/): Director of the Central Intelligence Agency under President Trump's first term; known to John Kiriakou and others at the CIA as "Bloody Gina"; per Kiriakou, flew out to the secret black site to…
- [Abu Zubaydah](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/abu-zubaydah/): Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized…
- [Espionage Act](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/espionage-act/): United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified…
- [Julian Assange](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/julian-assange/): Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.
- [John Brennan](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/john-brennan/): Former Director of the CIA; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as the principal architect of the agency's enhanced interrogation program and as having plotted against an elected President
- [MK-Ultra](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/mk-ultra/): The CIA's mid-twentieth-century umbrella program of mind-control, behavioral-modification, and biological-warfare experimentation, encompassing subprojects such as MK-Chickwit and MK-Seesaw;…
- [Vault 7](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/vault-7/): The 2017 WikiLeaks disclosure of thousands of pages of CIA Directorate of Science and Technology documents — leaked by agency engineer Joshua Schulte — revealing CIA technical capabilities…

- [Mad minute](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/mad-minute/): CIA case-officer procedure for the opening seconds of every meeting with a recruited source — confirm the source is safe, confirm a clean surveillance-detection route, and set the next meeting —…
- [Moral Injury](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/moral-injury/): Psychological diagnosis John Kiriakou received from a friend — a CIA veteran, brigadier general, and psychiatrist — who identified it as the source of Kiriakou's post-divorce PTSD.
- [Music as torture](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/music-as-torture/): The use of recorded music played on indefinite loop as a coercive interrogation technique.
- [Non-Personal Communication](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/non-personal-communication/): Per John Kiriakou, a category of espionage tradecraft encompassing all methods of passing information between an officer and an agent — or between two intelligence services — that do not require…
- [One-Time Pad](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/one-time-pad/): Cipher system in which a secret, random key — shared between sender and receiver — is used to encode a message and then destroyed so that it can never be used again.
- [Operating Directive](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/operating-directive/): The CIA's six-tier (0 through 5) intelligence priority system used to indicate the urgency with which case officers should pursue specific topics
- [Operational eating](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/kiriakou-operational-eating/): The two rules John Kiriakou gives about food on operations: that a case officer never orders seafood, and above all never shellfish, because a day spent incapacitated by food poisoning makes him…

### Agencies

- [Abraxas Corporation](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/abraxas-corporation/): The private intelligence company founded in the 1990s by retired CIA operations officers as a tax pass-through and a place to smoke cigars and tell stories — which, after 9/11, made its founders,…
- [Alex Station](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/alex-station/): CIA unit that tracked Osama bin Laden beginning in 1995; per John Kiriakou, who served as chief of its counterintelligence branch, the unit kept extremely tight security around its files, limited…
- [Bureau of Prisons](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/bureau-of-prisons/): The federal agency that ran John Kiriakou's incarceration — and one of his most persistent post-prison targets.
- [CIA directorates](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/cia-directorates/): The four-part internal division of the CIA as John Kiriakou describes it to lay audiences — the Directorate of Intelligence that analyses, the Directorate of Operations that recruits spies and…

- [Defense Intelligence Agency](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/defense-intelligence-agency/): The Pentagon's intelligence arm, of which John Kiriakou holds a low opinion he states plainly and expects to be criticised for.
- [From sixteen employees to twenty thousand](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/sixteen-employees-to-twenty-thousand/): John Kiriakou's support for cutting the staff of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, on the ground that a body created after 9/11 with sixteen employees to coordinate the agencies…

- [Gulf intelligence services](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/gulf-intelligence-services/): John Kiriakou's assessment of the intelligence services of the Gulf Cooperation Council states, which he worked with closely during his CIA career and rates uniformly excellent — highly trained,…

- [Houthis](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/houthis/): The Iran-aligned movement that controls the most important parts of Yemen, described by John Kiriakou as fierce fighters who beat the Saudi military over a decade of war and who in July 2026…
- [Iranian intelligence capability](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/iranian-intelligence-capability/): John Kiriakou's assessment of Iranian intelligence as poor and always having been poor, on the ground that Iranian officers do not receive good training and are essentially on their own, with only…
- [Irish intelligence services](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/irish-intelligence-services/): Ireland's intelligence and law-enforcement services, which John Kiriakou toured and met with during a speaking trip to Belfast, Cork, Dublin, and Waterford.

- [Office of the Director of National Intelligence](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/office-of-the-director-of-national-intelligence/): The intelligence-community layer created in 2004, which John Kiriakou argues should never have existed.
- [SAVAK](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/savak/): The intelligence service of the Shah of Iran, which John Kiriakou describes as bloodthirsty and as having spent far more effort investigating and murdering Iranian citizens than operating abroad.
- [Secret Service](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/secret-service/): The U.S. agency protecting the president. John Kiriakou, who worked alongside it for 35 years, describes a culture of complacency and poor follow-up — great with guns, weak on training and…

- [The Fifth Fleet in Bahrain](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/fifth-fleet/): The United States naval presence based in Bahrain since 1976 — the naval component of Central Command, headquartered at Manama.
- [The Gulf Daily News](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/gulf-daily-news/): Bahrain's English-language newspaper, and the source John Kiriakou turned to when a bomb went off at the Ministry of Labour two months into his posting — its Indian reporter, whose telephone was…

### Prosecution

- [Evidence of previous heroism](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/evidence-of-previous-heroism/): A phrase John Kiriakou attributes to Judge Leonie Brinkema at his 2013 sentencing.
- [Make it the blip](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/make-it-the-blip/): Having stayed up all night reading law review journals and concluded that he had broken no law, John Kiriakou telephoned his attorneys at six in the morning to say he wanted to go to trial.
- [Never meet my grandchildren](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/never-meet-my-grandchildren/): The threat John Kiriakou says one of the prosecutors in his case made to him — that he was going to die in prison and would never meet his grandchildren — set against the forty-five years he faced…
- [The 11(c)(1)(C) plea](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/the-eleven-c-one-c-plea/): The unusual plea structure John Kiriakou's lawyers negotiated in 2012, in which the sentence is written into the agreement and the judge may accept or reject it but cannot change it.
- [The contrition requirement](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/the-contrition-requirement/): The rule John Kiriakou says defeats his own pardon applications before they begin — that an applicant must show proof of contrition — and his refusal to meet it.
- [The threat to testify](https://www.kiripedia.org/wiki/the-threat-to-testify/): How John Kiriakou says he turned down the government''s "best and final" offer of ten years: by warning that he would have to take the stand in his own defence and might let slip the war crimes he…
